name: Gellan gum
aliases: E418, gellan gum, gellan, high-acyl gellan gum, low-acyl gellan gum, deacylated gellan gum, goma gellan
what_is: A high-molecular-weight polysaccharide produced by microbial fermentation and used as a gelling agent, stabiliser and thickener.
why_botia: Gellan gum is produced by fermentation and can form structure at very low concentrations, around 0.1%, much less than many other texturisers. That is why it is common in plant-based drinks: it helps keep calcium and other particles evenly distributed without making them too thick. It is not absorbed intact and, in high amounts, can have a laxative effect. JECFA did not see a need to set a numerical limit.
can_1: Identify E418 or gellan gum when declared on the label.
can_2: Trigger the E-number and texture information layers.
cannot_1: Determine whether the product uses a high-acyl or low-acyl grade unless the manufacturer states it.
cannot_2: Determine the quantity used or the detailed fermentation and purification conditions from the label.

sources.label: EU specifications for authorised food additives — Regulation (EU) No 231/2012
